chapters.title: Python Foundations for Data Work
learning_goals: Distinguish names, objects, values, and types.
Choose appropriate built-in data structures.
Use control flow, comprehensions, and functions for data tasks.
Handle errors and organize reusable code.
chapters.prerequisites: No previous programming experience; Python 3.10+ recommended.

chapters.title: Jupyter Notebook and Reproducible Workflows
learning_goals: Explain kernels, cells, execution order, and notebook metadata.
Use Markdown, code cells, magic commands, and rich display.
Restart and run notebooks from a clean state.
Control randomness and document dependencies.
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 1 Python fundamentals; JupyterLab or Jupyter Notebook.

chapters.title: CSV, JSON, and Excel Data Handling
learning_goals: Read and write CSV with the standard library and Pandas.
Parse JSON objects and arrays and understand serialization options.
Import/export Excel workbooks with Pandas and OpenPyXL.
Handle encodings, missing values, and data types.
chapters.prerequisites: Python file handling and basic DataFrame concepts.

chapters.title: APIs, Web Data, and Schema Validation
learning_goals: Explain URLs, methods, status codes, headers, query parameters, and timeouts.
Use Requests to retrieve and check API responses.
Parse HTML locally with BeautifulSoup.
Validate records with Pydantic and report malformed data.
chapters.prerequisites: Dictionaries, JSON, exceptions, and basic DataFrames; live internet access is optional.

chapters.title: NumPy: Numerical Computing
learning_goals: Explain ndarray shape, axes, dtype, and memory layout.
Create, index, slice, reshape, and combine arrays.
Use broadcasting, vectorized expressions, reductions, and masks.
Handle missing numeric values and reproducible random sampling.
chapters.prerequisites: Python lists, loops, functions, and arithmetic; install NumPy.

chapters.title: Pandas I: Series, DataFrames, and Inspection
learning_goals: Explain Series, DataFrame, index, columns, and alignment.
Read tabular data and inspect its structure.
Select rows and columns with loc and iloc.
Understand dtypes, missing values, and descriptive summaries.
chapters.prerequisites: Python and NumPy basics; install Pandas.

chapters.title: Pandas II: Cleaning, Transformation, and Aggregation
learning_goals: Diagnose missing values and duplicates.
Use string, datetime, and categorical accessors.
Transform with vectorized operations, map, and apply.
Group, aggregate, merge, concatenate, pivot, and melt.
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 6 DataFrame selection, dtypes, and inspection.

chapters.title: Polars and Apache Arrow for Efficient Data Processing
learning_goals: Explain eager versus lazy execution and query plans.
Use Polars expressions to select, filter, add, and aggregate columns.
Read files lazily and collect results deliberately.
Understand Arrow tables and interoperability.
chapters.prerequisites: Python, Pandas, SQL-style filtering/grouping; install `polars` and `pyarrow` for full examples.

chapters.title: SQL Fundamentals and MySQL Connectivity
learning_goals: Explain tables, rows, primary keys, and foreign keys.
Write SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, JOIN, and subqueries.
Connect with mysql-connector-python or PyMySQL.
Use parameterized statements, transactions, cursors, commits, and rollbacks.
chapters.prerequisites: Basic tables and Python functions. MySQL server only needed for live-connection exercises; SQLite is used for local SQL drills.

chapters.title: SQLAlchemy and Pandas Database Workflows
learning_goals: Distinguish Engine, Connection, Session, and ORM concepts.
Create database URLs and configure connection behavior.
Execute bound SQL with text().
Read and write DataFrames to relational databases safely.
chapters.prerequisites: Chapter 9 SQL. Install SQLAlchemy; MySQL driver is optional for the SQLite demonstrations.

chapters.title: Matplotlib: Foundational Data Visualization
learning_goals: Distinguish Figure and Axes objects.
Create line, bar, scatter, histogram, and box plots.
Control labels, scales, legends, grids, and layouts.
Export charts with readable dimensions and resolution.

chapters.title: Seaborn: Statistical Data Visualization
learning_goals: Understand long-form and wide-form data.
Use axes-level and figure-level plotting functions.
Create distribution, relational, categorical, and matrix plots.
Interpret hue, facets, estimators, and confidence intervals.
chapters.prerequisites: Pandas DataFrames and basic Matplotlib; install Seaborn.

chapters.title: Interactive Visualization with Plotly, Bokeh, and Altair
learning_goals: Build Plotly Express and Graph Objects charts.
Understand Bokeh figures, glyphs, sources, and tools.
Create declarative Altair charts and encodings.
Choose a library based on interaction, deployment, performance, and fit.
chapters.prerequisites: Pandas, Matplotlib concepts, and chart grammar; full stack includes Plotly, Bokeh, and Altair.

chapters.title: Scientific Statistics with SciPy
learning_goals: Select and parameterize continuous and discrete probability distributions.
Compute descriptive statistics and confidence intervals.
Choose and interpret common hypothesis tests.
Assess correlation and avoid common inferential errors.
chapters.prerequisites: NumPy arrays, Pandas filtering/grouping, and foundational probability concepts.

chapters.title: Statistical Modeling with Statsmodels
learning_goals: Fit and interpret ordinary least squares regression.
Use formulas and categorical variables safely.
Interpret coefficients, confidence intervals, p-values, and model fit.
Evaluate residual assumptions and recognize model limitations.
Understand the introductory workflow for time-series analysis.
chapters.prerequisites: Pandas, NumPy, descriptive statistics, and basic probability; SciPy statistics is recommended.

chapters.title: Exploratory Data Analysis and Data Quality
learning_goals: Define grain, keys, and quality rules before analyzing.
Profile missingness, duplicates, types, ranges, and categories.
Investigate outliers without blindly deleting them.
Explore univariate and multivariate structure.
Create a reproducible EDA summary and communicate caveats.
chapters.prerequisites: Pandas, NumPy, basic plotting, and introductory statistics.

chapters.title: Machine Learning with Scikit-learn
learning_goals: Define features, target, task type, and a baseline.
Split data before fitting transformations.
Build preprocessing and estimator pipelines.
Train regression and classification models.
Evaluate with task-appropriate metrics and cross-validation.
Recognize leakage, overfitting, and reproducibility requirements.
chapters.prerequisites: Python, NumPy, Pandas, descriptive statistics, and basic train/test reasoning.

chapters.title: Building Data Applications with Streamlit
learning_goals: Explain Streamlit’s script rerun model.
Build layouts with titles, columns, containers, and sidebar widgets.
Use caching appropriately for data and resources.
Connect CSV and MySQL data safely.
Structure, test, and deploy a small analytical application.
chapters.prerequisites: Python, Pandas, and at least one visualization library; install Streamlit separately.

chapters.title: End-to-End Data Analysis Capstone
learning_goals: Design a complete analytical workflow from a business question.
Load, validate, clean, and join multiple data sources.
Create reproducible metrics and statistical analyses.
Build visual findings and a simple predictive baseline.
Deliver a documented notebook, exported outputs, and dashboard-ready dataset.
chapters.prerequisites: Completion of the earlier foundations, processing, database, visualization, and analysis chapters.
